question: What are the two main pillars at the heart of Primary Health Care?
explanation: Primary Health Care is built on ensuring fair distribution and equal access to health services for all people. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T1#BMP117_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why does Primary Health Care focus on daily living conditions instead of only treating diseases?

options.A: International donors refuse to fund pure medical treatment programs
options.B: Doctors cannot diagnose illnesses accurately without community input
options.C: Medicines are too expensive for community health workers to distribute
options.D: Well-being depends on living conditions, environment, and social factors

explanation: Addressing root causes like poverty, housing, and sanitation prevents illness before medical treatment is even necessary. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T1#BMP117_U1_T1_h1)

question: What best describes the health programs used before Primary Health Care became the focus?

options.A: Rural maternity clinics run by local birth attendants
options.B: Comprehensive health systems based in village centers
options.D: Community-led initiatives focusing on general nutrition

explanation: Older vertical programs focused heavily on controlling one specific disease at a time without building lasting general health care systems. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T1#BMP117_U1_T1_h2)

question: What major problem with early hospital-centered health systems led to the creation of PHC?

options.A: Medical technology was too advanced for ordinary people to use
options.B: Hospitals were concentrated in cities, leaving rural areas unserved
options.C: Governments spent all their national budgets on purchasing ambulances
options.D: Doctors refused to treat patients who lived outside the capital city

explanation: Placing hospitals mainly in urban centers meant that most rural citizens had little to no access to basic medical care. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T1#BMP117_U1_T1_h2)

question: In which year was the historic International Conference on Primary Health Care held at Alma-Ata?
explanation: The Alma-Ata Declaration was adopted at the international conference held in September 1978. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T1#BMP117_U1_T1_h3)

question: What was the main global goal set by the Alma-Ata Declaration?

options.A: Health for All by the Year 2000
options.B: Complete elimination of traditional birth practices
options.C: Eradication of HIV across all nations
options.D: Universal free hospital care for children

explanation: The conference popularized the vision that basic health services should be universally available to every human being by the turn of the millennium. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T1#BMP117_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which principle states that local people must take part in planning their own health services?
explanation: Community participation ensures that health programs are designed with direct input from the people they serve. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T1#BMP117_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why does Primary Health Care need collaboration with fields like agriculture and education?

options.A: Agricultural ministries provide the funding required to build maternity wards
options.B: Health is influenced by factors outside the direct control of medical clinics
options.C: Doctors need extra assistance from teachers to manage hospital records
options.D: Schools are the only safe places to store vaccines in rural villages

explanation: Nutrition, literacy, and clean living environments directly shape health outcomes, so non-medical sectors must work alongside health providers. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T1#BMP117_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main role of a midwife working in a Nigerian Primary Health Care Centre?

options.A: Formulating national health insurance policies for government ministries
options.B: Providing frontline maternal and child health services at the grassroots
options.C: Managing international pharmaceutical supply chains for urban clinics
options.D: Conducting advanced surgical operations in tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Midwives in PHCs act as the first point of contact for pregnant women and children in local communities. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T1#BMP117_U1_T1_h5)

question: How does a Nigerian midwife apply the Alma-Ata principle of community participation in her work?

options.A: Ordering medical equipment directly from overseas manufacturers without consultation
options.B: Involving local women and leaders in planning health education and outreach programs
options.C: Requiring all pregnant women to relocate to city hospitals before delivery
options.D: Restricting clinic operations to standard administrative office hours only

explanation: Working closely with the local population respects community culture and encourages more women to use maternal health services. [learn more](BMP117_U1_T1#BMP117_U1_T1_h5)
